resources.string: Extract text locally instead of sending the raw file to a vision model — far cheaper in tokens. Good for PDFs, Word, and images with no people. Needs `pip install markitdown` on the machine.
Teach the machine your face and prove it is your machine. The face is what the LUKS/login watcher and the initramfs use to tell you from an intruder.
Arms `/face register` and sends a photo, which the machine stores as your template (and mirrors to the ESP so the initramfs can match it before boot).
I could not read that as an image. Pick a photo (JPG/PNG) of your face.
Fingerprint first: the enrolment is only armed and sent after you confirm it is really you on this phone.
I could not show the fingerprint prompt. Try again.
Also keep a copy in this phone
Saves the enrolment photo in the app\'s private data folder on this phone, as your own reference.
Saved a copy on this phone.
Runs /definehome: binds this machine\'s identity to its TPM, so it can prove it is your PC and not a clone.
Define this as MY phone (TrustZone / StrongBox)
Asking the machine to recognise this exact handset…

Registers with the machine over the pinned TLS 1.3 channel: the device key\'s attestation chain proves the key lives in this handset\'s secure hardware, so the machine can name you the owner instead of trusting the phone\'s word.
The machine has accepted this phone as yours, with its hardware attestation checked. Verdict: %1$s
This is already the handset the machine knows, and it re-checked the attestation. Verdict: %1$s
WARNING: the machine says this phone is a DIFFERENT handset than the one paired — the pairing secret has been copied. Verdict: %1$s
The machine refused to accept this phone\'s attestation. Verdict: %1$s
The machine returned an answer this app does not recognise (verdict: %1$s) — read it, and update the app.
No device key on this phone — every identify in this session has failed, so there is nothing the machine can attest.
Audio and video evidence captured at LUKS unlock and session start. Tap an item to play; the three-dot menu shows the hardware fingerprint and lets you export the log.
No evidence items yet. They appear here after the machine captures audio or video during unlock.
English is the default. Spanish is optional — this choice overrides the phone\'s own language for this app.
Turn each watcher on or off on the machine. The change is applied live and persisted by the daemon.
Pick the provider the machine asks, and which model answers. The daemon tries the provider live.
The model used when an image is involved. If your provider ships one model that does both (e.g. Gemini), put the same name here.
The phone\'s reference list of keys behind the models, each under an alias.

The machine keeps the active keys in its own config and never prints them. This is your reference copy on the phone — each key under the alias you choose, beside its provider, so it matches the model list. Keys are wrapped in this handset\'s secure hardware where available.
No keys saved yet. Add the first one below.
That alias is already in use.
This key can no longer be unwrapped — the keystore was reset. Tap the entry and re-enter it.
Stored without hardware wrapping on this handset.
Replaces the machine\'s entire system prompt (persona + hardware context). Leave empty to restore the default.

By design this app does not light up on its own: a phone that shows an alert while somebody is standing over you announces that the machine informed on you. Turn this on only if that trade is right for you.
Notifications are off in Android settings — grant the permission to receive alerts.

A direct connection to your machine: no relay, no server in between. The first time, get on the same WiFi as the PC and scan its QR. After that it does not matter where you are: the link does not expire, you only need to be able to reach the machine — same network, or your VPN. If the address changes, correct it here; there is no need to pair again.
Point at the QR the machine is showing
That QR is not one of ours, or something is missing from it (address, key, or the machine\'s TLS fingerprint). If the machine listens on 0.0.0.0, change it to the specific address.
There is an armed order waiting
Your fingerprint authorises it. No need to type the code.
This phone cannot sign: answer with %1$s.
Your fingerprint authorises this order and only this one.
Cancelled. The order stays armed until it expires.
Confirm this is really you before your face is sent to the machine.
The system did not return the signature; nothing was confirmed.
I could not sign the confirmation: %1$s
This phone cannot sign confirmations (no biometric enrolled, or no usable Keystore). Use the code.
Pair this phone with %1$s:%2$d\n\nand store the key and TLS fingerprint that came with the order.
Change the machine\'s address to %1$s:%2$d\n\nThe key and the pairing itself are untouched.
\n\nThis arrived in the intent that opened the app. If you did not just do this from a PC, say no.
Not paired — the machine and the key are missing
⚠️ The machine says this is NOT the phone it was paired with. If you did not re-pair it, somebody else has the pairing key.
no connection — cannot send it yet
no connection — the photo did not go out
no connection — I could not confirm

This pairing predates TLS on the channel and has no fingerprint for the machine stored.\n\nScan the QR again: I will not connect without being able to check that the thing answering is your machine and not another.
I could not connect to %1$s:%2$d.\n\nThis is a direct connection: there is no relay. Check that you are on the same network as the machine, or that the VPN is up.
I could not establish TLS with %1$s:%2$d.\n\n%3$s
This phone has no TLS 1.3. The machine speaks 1.3 only (so the connection reveals nothing to a watcher), and this handset is too old for it.

The machine's key is not the one you saved when pairing.

Expected %1$s
and got %2$s.

Either the daemon was reinstalled (and you need to pair again), or somebody is answering in its place.
This payload is %1$d bytes and the machine never accepts a frame over 1 MB. Pick a smaller file.
No log entries yet. Open the menu and send a report command, or tap Refresh.
the frame the daemon sent was too short to be valid

The frame did not authenticate.\n\nAlmost always this means the pairing key does not match the machine\'s. If the machine uses ChaCha20-Poly1305 (a CPU with no hardware AES), this phone needs Android 9 or later.
